data.title: Hedge Funds’ US Natural Gas Shorts Reach Record on Warm-Winter Bets
data.description: Hedge funds amassed their largest-ever short position in US natural gas this week, betting an unusually warm winter will cut demand for the fuel used by furnaces and power plants, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: JPMorgan: U.S. Treasury Bill Demand May Not Keep Pace With 2027 Supply
data.description:
JPMorgan strategists Jay Barry, Pankaj Vohra and others said U.S. Treasury bill issuance is expected to keep expanding, with the market needing to absorb $991 billion in net supply in 2027, making demand’s ability to keep pace a key question. According to Sina Finance, the strategists see some headwinds: They expect money market fund assets under management to grow at roughly the pace seen during the larger inflows in 2024 or 2025, unless a major market disruption comparable to the 2020 pandemic shock or 2023 regional banking stress occurs.

The strategists said foreign official investors’ recent pullback has been tactical rather than structural, leaving room for them to resume a steadier pace of short-term Treasury purchases. They said a similar recovery is unlikely in the stablecoin sector unless cryptocurrencies rebound or the regulatory environment becomes clearer. Treasury bill valuations are unlikely to reverse sharply to more expensive levels next year, and pressure may be particularly evident during the 2027 supply increase as money markets absorb the additional bills and demand may grow more slowly than in previous years.

The strategists said lower bill valuations could also affect funding markets, particularly if money market funds sharply reduce repo allocations to buy more bills or funding markets become more sensitive to bill settlement dates. The debt ceiling could begin to factor in next spring, when the U.S. Treasury may reduce its general account balance, making funding market conditions harder to assess. Money market fund assets under management have stalled over the past two months. Although the strategists expect a seasonal rebound during the rest of 2026, they project growth of only about 5% for the year, compared with double-digit growth in each of the previous two years.

In the four months through August, foreign investors reduced their holdings of short-term U.S. Treasuries by about $145 billion, bringing foreign official investors’ share of holdings to 4.3%, its lowest level since May 2024. Stablecoin growth has also stalled this year. Fiat-backed stablecoin supply has fluctuated between $265 billion and $280 billion, while stablecoin holdings of Treasury bills total $127 billion, or 2% of all Treasury bills, down from $137 billion in December 2025.

data.title: Nationwide and MFS Funds Face Large Capital Gains Distributions in 2026
data.description: According to CNBC, the Nationwide Renaissance Small Cap Growth Fund (NWGPX) is estimated to distribute 56.6% of its net asset value in capital gains, while the A-share version of the MFS Global Equity Fund (MWEFX) is set to distribute 31% to 33%. Morningstar senior manager research analyst Stephen Welch compiled a list of funds with the highest estimated distributions for 2026. Fund families expect to make the distributions in December. Investors holding the funds in taxable brokerage accounts may owe long-term capital gains taxes at rates of 0%, 15% or 20%, depending on taxable income; holdings in tax-deferred accounts such as IRAs and 401(k)s are not affected. Investors can use tax-loss harvesting to offset capital gains, and may direct distributions to cash rather than reinvesting them.

data.title: STOCKS | TSX Posts Steepest Drop Since June in North American Retreat
data.description: The TSX had its sharpest decline since June as technology and materials stocks weighed on the benchmark, joining a broader North American retreat, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: STOCKS | Apple Regains World's Highest Valuation, Surpassing Nvidia
data.description: Apple reclaimed its position as the world's most valuable company on Friday, overtaking Nvidia as investors sought the perceived safety of the iPhone maker amid concerns about artificial intelligence spending, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: AstraZeneca Shares Jump Nearly 7% on Earnings Beat and $1.5 Billion Savings Plan
data.description: AstraZeneca shares rose nearly 7% on Friday after beating third-quarter earnings forecasts and announcing a restructuring plan. Third-quarter revenue rose 7% to $16.21 billion and core earnings were $2.79 per share, above the $2.59 estimate, according to BeInCrypto. Oncology revenue rose 17%, while Farxiga sales fell 25% amid generic competition; a breast cancer trial missed its main target and a lung cancer study was stopped. The plan targets $1.5 billion in annual savings, with up to $2 billion in upfront costs, for a pipeline of more than 180 projects. AstraZeneca acquired Modella AI and partnered with insitro; CEO Pascal Soriot targets $80 billion in annual revenue by 2030. Shares closed above £131.34, with chart targets of £145.38 and £157.30.

data.title: Blackstone Expects Junk Rating for Anthropic, Clouding Its $800 Billion AI Bet
data.description: Blackstone now expects Anthropic to receive a junk rating after its record IPO, reversing its earlier forecast of investment-grade status by year-end. The shift, based on feedback from major agencies, puts borrowing costs for Anthropic’s more than $800 billion compute plan in focus, according to BeInCrypto. KBRA rated Anthropic BB+ in June. In Project North Star’s $63 billion chip financing, Broadcom guarantees more than $42 billion, while Anthropic alone backs $18 billion, including about $9 billion held by Blackstone funds at yields above 10%. Fitch, Moody’s and S&P have not ruled; their decision after the Nasdaq debut, expected by late November, will affect borrowing costs.

data.title: Meta Settles With Teen in Trial Over Social Media Harm Claims
data.description: According to CNBC, Meta Platforms settled on Friday with K.D.B., an 18-year-old plaintiff who alleged that Instagram and Facebook were designed to be addictive and caused her mental health problems and disordered eating. The settlement followed the start of jury selection on Wednesday in a trial against Meta and Snap Inc. The case is expected to proceed against Snap only after Meta settled with K.D.B. and had previously settled with the other teen plaintiff, S.J.

data.title: STOCKS | Vail Resorts Gets Baron Capital Backing in Proxy Fight With Oasis
data.description: Baron Capital, one of Vail Resorts Inc.’s largest shareholders, is backing the company and its nominees as it faces a proxy fight with activist investor Oasis Management, according to Bloomberg.
